summary: This article explains how gravity, spin, air pressure, friction, and good jumping form explain shooting, bouncing, and moving in basketball.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “The Science of Basketball”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: a curved path or shape, like part of a circle
the direction or slant at which something moves or meets something else
a backward turning of a ball as it moves forward

challengeTerms.def: the curved path an object follows as it moves through the air
able to stretch or squeeze and then return to its original shape
the force that keeps a moving object moving

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that knowing science can make you a better athlete? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how two different science ideas from the article help a player make a basket.
struggling: Pre-teach arc, angle, and backspin with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use trajectory, elastic, and momentum in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
